title: Late only once, with Elliott Lawrence's show, and Freddie Webster
summary: Crawford says he was late once in 45 years, during a Broadway show, and recalls Freddie Webster could not keep time.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Now, did this cause any problems between you all and Lukoford?

No, long as we were there on time. You know, Stan, I never miss time. That's why right today I have a natural habit of looking at a clock. All day long I look at a clock, checking that time. I was only late one time in my career, and that was when I was playing a show with Elliott Lawrence conducting.
Well, I was laying in bed and --
(Inaudible).
-- when the time changed, went ahead, went from -- daylight savings something.
From 730 to 830
No, they changed time (inaudible) for a short while.
Well, they had daylight saving time,
Alone. That's what caused me to miss, be late.
They changed the time of (Inaudible) the Broadway shows, from 7:30 to 8:30 (inaudible) and he was thinking it was still 8:30.
Uh-huh, so --
And they held up the show for a half an hour --

Let me -- I'm recording, Alone. He's got his machine on here. So I was late. I was late. I don't care what she's saying. Maybe they pushed the time up for the Broadway show. And so Elliott Lawrence called up here, saying where's Jimmie. We're waiting on him down here. I jumped out of bed and got dressed in nothing flat, didn't take a shower, nothing, went in that -- got in that pit.

And so in the meantime Elliott Lawrence had announced on the loudspeaker to the audience, ladies and gentlemen, we're sorry we can't go on on time like we were supposed to. Our drummer is not here. Now, wasn't that a what in the heck of a thing? was that? Our drummer's not here.
(Inaudible).
And so -- wait a minute. Who's recording this thing? And so I finally got there, sweating, everything. And so the show went on.
So with 45 years of playing you've only been late once?
One time.
That's incredible.

And, you know, we had a trumpet player in the band in later years by the name of Freddie Webster. Oh, that man was atrociously -- atrociously -- just couldn't do right. He overblown. He came to me one time and asked me, hey, Craw, tell me. How in the world can you always be on time? He said, that's going against the grain. I said, well, we were taught to be on time. I was glad he left the band.
